gap: No result ChatGPT got states DashCamTalk's figures for the Vantrue OnDash N4 (15.3 + 8.3 + 6.7 Mb/s for front, rear and cabin, night video 5/10), nor that it is the only 3-channel camera at or under $100 with any named-reviewer measurement.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages and nine other results. Digital Camera World's budget guide (cited) names no 3-channel camera and no measured figure in the part I could read (the fetch was truncated); the cited Walmart browse page was not opened. deal.ai, cabincommand, dashcamempire, productbible, offkeytikki and roadgearlab carry no named measurement of any 3-channel camera at this price. But us.my-best.com/22269 (rank 12 in the second chat, not cited) already holds in-house test results for the N4: 4.27/5 overall, low light 4.47/5, measured field of view 100° front against 155° claimed. So a result already has part of the angle; only the bitrate, the storage arithmetic and DashCamTalk's night score are new. caranddriver.com could not be opened; its AOL syndicated copy has no N4 and no 3-channel camera under $100.
decides: It supports the Vantrue OnDash N4 over ChatGPT's REDTIGER A3 on evidence, if the N4 is still $99.99 (I could not read Vantrue's store today). The N4 has three independent tests (DashCamTalk, mybest, Digital Camera World); I found none for the A3 and did not search for the TOGUARD or Odrey. The measurements also set the N4's limits: DashCamTalk rates night video 5/10 with the rear camera below average at night, mybest measured the front view at 100°, there is no Wi-Fi or app, and GPS needs a separate mount. The A3 is $27.25 cheaper at Redtiger's store with Wi-Fi and, by ChatGPT's Walmart card, a 32 GB card, so it is the price pick resting on maker claims only.

findings.label: Bitrate per channel (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 15.3 Mb/s front, 8.3 Mb/s rear, 6.7 Mb/s cabin
findings.note: Review published 2020-09-22. Front and rear figures are in the spec table under 'Bitrate'; the cabin figure is in the body text. The page does not say whether they were measured from footage or taken from the maker.

findings.label: Recording time per card, from DashCamTalk's bitrates (our arithmetic)
findings.value: about 13.6 GB per hour with all three cameras; about 18.8 hours on a 256 GB card, 9.4 hours on 128 GB
findings.note: 15.3 + 8.3 + 6.7 = 30.3 Mb/s; × 3,600 s = 109,080 Mb = 13,635 MB ≈ 13.6 GB per hour; 256 ÷ 13.635 = 18.8 h. Video only, decimal GB, audio and file overhead ignored. The 256 GB maximum is from mybest's spec table, not from Vantrue's page.

findings.label: DashCamTalk ratings
findings.value: Day video 7/10, night video 5/10, reliability 8/10, discreetness 6/10, value 8/10, support 6/10
findings.note: Rated 2020-09-22 at a $260 price. Quotes: front 'good video quality during the day and average quality at night'; rear 'average during the day and below average night'; interior 'very good in the day and average at night'. 'There are no common problems reported with this camera.'

findings.label: Three-channel resolution, size, temperature, Wi-Fi, GPS (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 2560 × 1440 front at 30 fps + 1080p rear at 30 fps + 1080p cabin; 108 × 45 × 45 mm; -10 °C to 70 °C; supercapacitor; no Wi-Fi; GPS mount optional
findings.note: Sensors are listed as Sony STARVIS on all three cameras with no model numbers. The page names the processor two ways (Hi3559 V200 in the text, Hi3556 V200 in the table). No frame rate is given for the cabin camera.

findings.label: mybest in-house test scores (8 three-channel cameras)
findings.value: 4.27/5 overall, ranked 3rd of 8; high light 4.77, low light 4.47 (second of 8), interior camera 3.97, field of view 4.70, app usability 3.00, SD card error prevention 3.50
findings.note: Method: front and rear cameras shot a license plate at 12, 16 and 32 ft and ten testers read it; low light at about 0.1 lux with a lamp simulating a tunnel exit, plate at 6.5 ft; default settings. Quote: 'We were able to clearly record the numbers on license plates in both good and bad conditions.' Scored at a $259.99 reference price. No test date on the page. Scores come from the fetch tool's summary, not checked against the raw page.

findings.label: Measured horizontal field of view (mybest) against the listed figure
findings.value: Measured 100° front, 100° rear, 120° cabin; listed 155° front, 160° rear, 165° cabin
findings.note: Protractor and chalk lines, cones at 10° steps from 40° to 130°, so 130° is the test's ceiling. Listed angles are usually diagonal, so the two are not like for like. The same test measured 100° front on the VIOFO T130 and A229 Pro and 90° on the AZDOME M550.

findings.label: Conflict between sources on cabin and rear resolution
findings.value: mybest's table: 1440P front, 1080P rear, 1440P cabin; DashCamTalk and Digital Camera World: 1440p + 1080p + 1080p with all three recording
findings.note: mybest's frame-rate row carries the footnote 'Dual recording mode', so its table may describe front + cabin mode. Use Vantrue's own three-channel figure on the page.

findings.label: Digital Camera World review (Amy Davies)
findings.value: 1440p + 1080p + 1080p with all three recording, 30 fps maximum; 4K from the front camera alone; parking mode needs hardwiring and was 'not something we've been able to test'
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 dashcam review | Digital Camera World
findings.note: Published 2021-10-30. No instrument measurements. Quote: 'generally enough detail to see important details - such as numberplates'. Night video and heat are not covered.
